subject.title: [Bug]: exec / read tools mangle GBK-encoded output on Windows (cp936), corrupting transcript and causing empty-response loop

question: Should the shared Windows decoder keep whole-buffer automatic legacy fallback, or should it adopt a narrower strategy that preserves valid UTF-8 segments while retaining explicit support for complete CP936 output?
rationale: The report plausibly exposes a real decoder-policy edge case, but mixed or truncated buffers make the compatibility contract broader than a mechanical one-line fix.

options.title: Approve a narrow fallback repair
options.body: Preserve complete legacy-code-page decoding, but change the fallback decision only after Windows CP936 proof demonstrates correct UTF-8 and GBK behavior.

options.title: Keep the current heuristic
options.body: Retain whole-buffer fallback if maintainers judge mixed-buffer behavior too ambiguous, while documenting the supported encoding contract.

options.title: Split recovery behavior first
options.body: Track the empty-response and failed-session sequence separately if it reproduces after correct tool decoding.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow fallback repair
recommendation.body: Preserve complete legacy-code-page decoding, but change the fallback decision only after Windows CP936 proof demonstrates correct UTF-8 and GBK behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared decoding behavior appears to originate in the Windows process-output work introduced by this contributor.
